observation.happening: Slack message confirmation dialog in dark theme. User is reviewing a message before sending it to #sales channel.
observation.most_important: Clear confirmation state with orange 'send' button that dominates visual hierarchy. Full message content visible with recipient, channel, and timestamp clearly shown.
observation.next_action: User can confirm send, edit, or cancel the message.

51F1.why: Flawlessly executed confirmation dialog with excellent visual hierarchy and button placement. However, the pattern is entirely standard — confirmation dialogs are familiar and this adds no distinctive elements beyond competent execution.

observation.happening: macOS app home screen greeting user with time-of-day phrase. Shows sidebar navigation (Home/Work/Library/Apps) and main content area with input field and expandable feature cards.
observation.most_important: Greeting screen with empty state gracefully handled. Input prompt is clear. Instructional content is well-organized in collapsed sections.
observation.next_action: User can enter what they want to finish, expand feature cards, or navigate to other sections.
anomalies: Explanatory text boxes create visual density in what should be a calm empty state

5471.why: Well-crafted macOS native app with excellent whitespace and calm aesthetic. The sidebar + main content layout is completely standard. Explanatory boxes feel somewhat instructional rather than effortlessly discoverable. Good craft but no distinctive design choices.

visible_text: Q4 移行計画の打ち合わせ

observation.happening: Active recording session shown with inline card at top of screen. Pink/salmon background indicates recording is live. Timer shows 00:01, status label says '録音中' (recording). Card contains action buttons (memo, Ask Astra, stop).
observation.most_important: Recording state is unmistakably clear through color, icon (red dot), text label, and timer. Card design creates visual separation from the rest of content flow.
observation.next_action: User can open memo, ask Astra, or stop recording. Can also review recent meetings below.

598B.why: Well-designed inline notification for active recording with strong state clarity. The card-based approach to showing recording context is thoughtful. However, the overall layout still follows familiar patterns (notification card + list below). Pink background is slightly assertive rather than calming.

visible_text: 前回の設定でその場で録り始めます
Q4 移行計画の打ち合わせ

observation.happening: Home screen now populated with upcoming meetings in 'これからの予定' (upcoming schedule) section. Shows two calendar events with times, platforms, and red 'record' badges.
observation.most_important: Upcoming meetings are clearly displayed with consistent layout. Each meeting shows title, time, platform, and recording toggle. State is predictable.
observation.next_action: User can click on meetings to interact, or start recording from any upcoming meeting. Can expand other sections above.

5F3B.why: Same screen layout as 5471 now with data populated. Meetings list is clean and readable with consistent styling. The design is functionally sound but uses entirely standard list patterns. Excellent whitespace maintains calmness, but no distinctive design choices.

observation.happening: Floating control bar for active recording session showing pause state. Dark gray bar with status, timer, and quick-access buttons arranged horizontally.
observation.most_important: Pause state is clear with text label. Timer is prominent. All essential controls (memo, transcript, Ask Astra, play, record) fit in minimal space without crowding.
observation.next_action: User can resume, access memo/transcript/Astra, or access recording controls.

6479.why: Perfectly minimalist floating control bar. Absolutely no wasted space — every element is functional and purposefully placed. Horizontal layout is ideal for floating window. State is unmistakably clear. Density and geometry are exceptional. This could stand next to professional tools like Apple's recording controls. No defects or unnecessary elements.

observation.happening: Apps screen showing Connectors tab. Three connector cards displayed horizontally: Gmail (needs auth), Google Calendar (needs auth), and Finder (ready to use). Each card shows service icon, status, and explanation.
observation.most_important: Connector status is clear for each service. Gmail and Google Calendar both show 'must configure' status (red badge), Finder shows 'ready' status (blue badge). Tab navigation shows Plugins/Connectors options.
observation.next_action: User can click each connector to set up authentication or manage connections.

6649.why: Standard connector marketplace pattern — three cards in horizontal layout showing integration status. State clarity is excellent with clear status badges. However, the overall composition is entirely familiar. This is well-executed but not distinctive compared to marketplace patterns in Linear, Zapier, or similar tools.
